finding_definitions.cardiomegaly: Cardiomegaly is an enlarged heart: the finding is the cardiac silhouette itself, wider than normal for the chest, so its box is the heart shadow.
finding_definitions.pleural effusion: A pleural effusion is fluid layering at the lung base, blunting the costophrenic angle and obscuring the hemidiaphragm, so it sits low in the chest.
finding_definitions.pneumothorax: A pneumothorax is air in the pleural space, a lucent rim without lung markings, most often at the lung apex.
finding_definitions.consolidation: Consolidation is airspace filling that turns part of the lung dense and opaque; it lies within the lung fields.
finding_definitions.pneumonia: Pneumonia appears as a patchy or confluent opacity within the lung fields.
finding_definitions.atelectasis: Atelectasis is collapsed lung, increased density with volume loss, typically in a lower zone or near the diaphragm.
finding_definitions.edema: Pulmonary edema is fluid in the lung, a hazy opacity spreading from the hila across the lung fields.
finding_definitions.lung opacity: A lung opacity is a region of lung denser than normal aerated lung.

anatomical_definitions.cardiac silhouette: The cardiac silhouette is the heart shadow: the dense white mass low in the center of the chest, most of it to the patient's left, resting on the diaphragm.
anatomical_definitions.left cardiac silhouette: The left cardiac silhouette is the part of the heart shadow on the patient's left of the midline, most of the heart's bulk.
anatomical_definitions.right cardiac silhouette: The right cardiac silhouette is the part of the heart shadow on the patient's right of the midline, its border formed by the right atrium.
anatomical_definitions.left lung: The left lung is the whole dark aerated field on the patient's left, from the apex above the clavicle down to the diaphragm.
anatomical_definitions.right lung: The right lung is the whole dark aerated field on the patient's right, from the apex above the clavicle down to the diaphragm.
anatomical_definitions.left upper lung zone: The left upper lung zone is the top third of the left lung, from the apex down to about the level of the hilum.
anatomical_definitions.right upper lung zone: The right upper lung zone is the top third of the right lung, from the apex down to about the level of the hilum.
anatomical_definitions.left mid lung zone: The left mid lung zone is the middle third of the left lung, the band around the level of the hilum.
anatomical_definitions.right mid lung zone: The right mid lung zone is the middle third of the right lung, the band around the level of the hilum.
anatomical_definitions.left lower lung zone: The left lower lung zone is the bottom third of the left lung, from below the hilum down to the diaphragm.
anatomical_definitions.right lower lung zone: The right lower lung zone is the bottom third of the right lung, from below the hilum down to the diaphragm.
anatomical_definitions.left apical zone: The left apical zone is the very top of the left lung, the small cap of lung at and above the level of the clavicle.
anatomical_definitions.right apical zone: The right apical zone is the very top of the right lung, the small cap of lung at and above the level of the clavicle.
anatomical_definitions.left hilar structures: The left hilar structures are the vessels and airways entering the left lung: the dense shadow where the lung meets the mediastinum, at mid-height.
anatomical_definitions.right hilar structures: The right hilar structures are the vessels and airways entering the right lung: the dense shadow where the lung meets the mediastinum, at mid-height.
anatomical_definitions.left costophrenic angle: The left costophrenic angle is the sharp corner where the left hemidiaphragm meets the chest wall, at the outer bottom edge of the left lung.
anatomical_definitions.right costophrenic angle: The right costophrenic angle is the sharp corner where the right hemidiaphragm meets the chest wall, at the outer bottom edge of the right lung.
anatomical_definitions.left cardiophrenic angle: The left cardiophrenic angle is the corner where the heart shadow meets the left hemidiaphragm, near the midline at the bottom of the chest.
anatomical_definitions.right cardiophrenic angle: The right cardiophrenic angle is the corner where the heart shadow meets the right hemidiaphragm, near the midline at the bottom of the chest.
anatomical_definitions.left hemidiaphragm: The left hemidiaphragm is the domed white line under the left lung, the top surface of the diaphragm on that side.
anatomical_definitions.right hemidiaphragm: The right hemidiaphragm is the domed white line under the right lung, usually a little higher than the left, the top surface of the diaphragm on that side.
anatomical_definitions.trachea: The trachea is the dark air column running down the midline of the upper chest, from the neck to the carina.
anatomical_definitions.carina: The carina is the point where the trachea splits into the two main bronchi, in the midline near the center of the chest.
anatomical_definitions.mediastinum: The mediastinum is the central compartment between the two lungs, from the neck down to the diaphragm, holding the heart and great vessels.
anatomical_definitions.upper mediastinum: The upper mediastinum is the central soft-tissue band between the lungs above the heart, holding the trachea and the great vessels.
anatomical_definitions.svc: The svc is the superior vena cava: the straight vessel border running down the patient's right edge of the upper mediastinum into the right atrium.
anatomical_definitions.cavoatrial junction: The cavoatrial junction is where the superior vena cava meets the right atrium, on the patient's right heart border.
anatomical_definitions.right atrium: The right atrium forms the patient's right border of the heart shadow, the curve on the right side of the cardiac silhouette.
anatomical_definitions.aortic arch: The aortic arch is the rounded knob on the patient's left edge of the upper mediastinum, just above the heart.
anatomical_definitions.descending aorta: The descending aorta is the vertical vessel edge running down behind the heart, just to the patient's left of the spine.
anatomical_definitions.spine: The spine is the vertebral column: the stack of vertebrae running down the midline of the chest, behind the heart and mediastinum.
anatomical_definitions.left clavicle: The left clavicle is the collarbone crossing the top of the chest on the patient's left, a near-horizontal bone over the lung apex.
anatomical_definitions.right clavicle: The right clavicle is the collarbone crossing the top of the chest on the patient's right, a near-horizontal bone over the lung apex.
anatomical_definitions.abdomen: The abdomen is the area below both hemidiaphragms at the bottom of the image, under the lung bases.
anatomical_definitions.left upper abdomen: The left upper abdomen is the region just below the left hemidiaphragm, under the left lung base; the stomach air bubble often sits there.
anatomical_definitions.right upper abdomen: The right upper abdomen is the region just below the right hemidiaphragm, under the right lung base, occupied by the liver.

marker_outside_clause: It sits outside every key anatomical location; markers placed outside the body usually appear near the image border or a corner.
marker_appearance: The marker is an artificial object pasted onto the image, typically brighter than the surrounding anatomy, with sharp edges and no fixed shape or size.
region_edges_clause: On this image the {region} spans y = {ry0} to {ry1} and x = {rx0} to {rx1}, and {share} the {name} lies within that window.
coordinate_convention: On the image grid, y runs from 0 at the top to {max} at the bottom, and x from 0 at the image's left, the patient's right, to {max} at the image's right, the patient's left; the upper, middle and lower thirds of the image are split at y = {third} and y = {two_thirds}, and {x_cuts}.

x_cuts.band: the central band around the midline runs from x = {band_lo} to x = {band_hi}
x_cuts.span: a box spans the midline when it reaches past x = {span_lo} and x = {span_hi}

edges_bbox: Its edges are y0 = {y0}, y1 = {y1}, x0 = {x0}, x1 = {x1}.
coord_restate_bbox: The queried box has top edge y0 = {y0}, bottom edge y1 = {y1} and side edges x0 = {x0}, x1 = {x1}.
coord_deduction: Its {y_from_clause}, so the point occupies {vertical}; its {x_from_clause}, so it is {horizontal}.
coord_deduction_bbox: Its y span {y_case}, so the box occupies {vertical}; its x span {x_case}, so it is {horizontal}.

span_case.crosses: crosses {line} with its larger share in {part}
span_case.tie: crosses {line} with equal shares on either side, counted as {part}

quadrant_axis_bbox.tie: its {axis} span sits equally on both sides of {axis} = {half}, counted as {axis} {rel} {half}

quadrant_clause: {y_phrase} and {x_phrase}, so it falls in the patient's {quadrant}{suffix}.
coord_region_clause: That part of this image is the {region}{within}.
coord_outside_clause: That spot lies outside every key anatomical location.
coord_outside_marker_prior: Markers placed outside the body usually appear near the image border or a corner.
coord_negative_clause: No key anatomical location, marker, or finding overlaps that spot.
coord_marker_appearance: A marker is an artificial object pasted onto the image, typically brighter than the surrounding anatomy, with sharp edges.
